title: Lost Mass? Chemical Laws Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A candle seems to lose mass as it burns, an iron gate gets heavier as it rusts, and pure water is always the same wherever it comes from. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 1, Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry) Aarav finds rust on his bicycle chain and five old laws explain all three puzzles.

You will see conservation of mass (Antoine Lavoisier, 1789) on a closed flask, definite proportions (Joseph Proust) with natural and lab made copper carbonate (51.35% copper, 9.74% carbon, 38.91% oxygen), and multiple proportions (John Dalton, 1803) built on the molecule bench as water and hydrogen peroxide share electrons: 16 g and 32 g of oxygen for the same 2 g of hydrogen, a 1 : 2 ratio. Then Gay Lussac's law of gaseous volumes (1808) and Avogadro's law (1811) step by step, with gas volumes splitting into water molecules, a worked example on CO and CO2, all five laws side by side, the exam trap about candles, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 6 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:

1:18 Law 3: multiple proportions on the bench

3:17 Worked example: CO and CO2
3:48 All five laws
